# Post-training

Manipulation Action Models → Multi-Fingered Dexterous Hand Manipulation Research → Tactile Manipulation → Post-training

Adapt pretrained manipulation models with tactile or force observations and contact-aware objectives. Specify which expert receives measured history, whether future contact is a training target or an execution command, and which components are updated during training. | [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.14] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-14"></a> | **DexTacWAM｜WAM architecture · World-model-side tactile input · Joint visual–tactile prediction**<br>[DexTacWAM: A Visuo-Tactile World-Action Model for Dexterous Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.24976v1)<br>Haoran Yuan, Zekai Wang, Boning Shao, Haoran Lu, Trevor Darrell, Ismini Lourentzou, Wei Zhan<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` `wam` [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `visuo-tactile-world-model` `future-tactile-prediction` `contact-dynamics` `finger-and-pose-aware-compression` `predictive-feature-action-generation` `modality-wise-kv-normalization` `continual-vision-to-touch-learning` `flow-matching` `imitation-learning` `action-chunking` `real-world` `tactile-post-training` `world-model-tactile-input` | DexTacWAM compresses ten fingertip streams into two hand latents and adds them as extra views to a pretrained video world model, jointly predicting future images and contact evolution; an action expert then reads predictive visual–tactile features to generate arm–hand actions.<br>**Evaluation scope:** A frozen visual VAE encodes each fingertip; finger identity, hand pose and temporal refinement compress five streams per hand into one latent. The action expert separately normalizes visual/tactile K/V before cross-attention. Training adapts the tactile encoder on 488 interactions, finetunes the world model on about 100 demonstrations per task, then jointly trains it and a new action expert on those demonstrations, without RL. Roughly four hours refers to recorded data, not training time. Deployment uses one world-model forward pass for predictive features, without fully rendering futures or searching trajectories. The 194-D target includes arm/hand actions, finger-force and next-proprioception predictions, not 194 joints; forces are training supervision, not deployment inputs or demonstrated direct force control. Six real-robot tasks on a dual-Sharpa-Wave platform cover occluded cube placement, handover, wiping, tongs/tomato transfer, bowl unstacking and cap unscrewing, with 20 trials per method/task. The 70.6 average mixes binary and staged scores. Removing tactile world prediction drops the controlled four-task mean from 74.7 to 26.6. Models are trained per task; cross-hand transfer is untested. Release status checked on 2026-10-28: the official repository provides training/deployment code, the 488-episode corpus, six task datasets and tactile-encoder weights, explicitly excluding task-specific world-model and action-expert checkpoints. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.24976v1) · [Project](https://dextacwam.github.io/) · [Code](https://github.com/dextacwam/DexTacWAM) · [Data](https://huggingface.co/collections/JensenYuan/dextacwam) · [Assets](https://huggingface.co/JensenYuan/DexTacWAM_multi_finger_tactile_encoder) | Initial reading<br>2026-11-04 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.PLANNING.3] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-planning-3"></a> | **Motus2｜WAM architecture · Tactile-expert post-training · Sub-chunk action denoising refinement**<br>[Motus2: A Self-Evolving General World Model for Dexterous Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.30237v2)<br>Hongzhe Bi, Zihao Zhou, Yihang Tang, Jingrui Pang, Shuhe Huang, Haitian Liu, Runqing Wang, Shuai Huang, Yichen Wang, Yiming Cheng, Ruowen Zhao, Zhenghua Li, Hengkai Tan, Xiaolong Liu, Jinhui Wan, Jiabao Liu, Min Zhao, Fan Bao, Jun Zhu<br>[Canonical paper entry](../policies/world-model-planning.md#am-man-dex-policy-planning-3)<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` `wam` `general-world-model` `shared-policy-simulator-evaluator` `model-based-rl` [reinforcement-learning](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `diffusion-nft` `value-guided-planning` `best-of-n` `egocentric-human-pretraining` [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `tactile-post-training` `tactile-expert` `tactile-action-refinement` `future-force-prediction` `flow-matching` `action-chunking` `working-memory` `real-world` | Motus2 post-trains a lightweight tactile expert on an existing world–action backbone, reusing intermediate actions and cached backbone features to finish denoising each sub-chunk with fresh touch immediately before execution, with auxiliary future-force prediction during training.<br>**Evaluation scope:** The main entry emphasizes the shared policy–simulator–evaluator and value-guided improvement under world-model planning; the tactile entry emphasizes adapting an existing backbone through expert post-training. Initialized from Wan 2.2-TI2V-5B, the backbone undergoes monocular video pretraining, stereo video–human-action pretraining and robot-domain adaptation. Its action-first mask prevents actions from reading same-chunk future video or value. Successful demonstrations supervise actions, while failures/suboptimal trajectories inform dynamics and value learning. Ordinary deployment can generate actions alone; Best-of-N additionally simulates and scores candidates, replanning from real observations without weight updates. DiffusionNFT MBRL instead updates action-related parameters while freezing the video backbone and evaluator. Its asynchronous pipeline is for training, not asynchronous WAM deployment. The tactile expert reads detached intermediate actions, layer-wise K/V caches and the latest tactile window. A 48-step chunk is first denoised to noise level 0.2, then divided into eight six-action sub-chunks of about 0.2 seconds for sequential final denoising. Tactile losses update only the expert, force encoder/decoder and applicable deformation encoder. Sharpa Wave inputs are 60D bimanual force/torque and ten fingertip deformation images; Wuji Hand 2 uses 1086D pointwise and per-finger force signals. Future force is an auxiliary training target; deformation images are conditioning inputs only. Deployment outputs refined actions, not force-control references. Tactile comparisons use 20 trials each on paper-cup extraction with Sharpa and paper tearing with Wuji Hand 2, improving 65%/55% to 75%/70%; these do not establish same-task cross-hand transfer. Separate 20-trial/task MBRL/planning comparisons on Put Phone and Multi-Finger improve the mean from 65% to 75% with both enabled; these results must not be conflated with the tactile study. | arXiv v2 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.30237v2) · [Project](https://motus-robotics.github.io/motus2/) | Initial reading<br>2026-11-04 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.TACTILE.POSTTRAIN.1] <a id="am-man-dex-tactile-posttrain-1"></a> | **InternW0｜WAM architecture · AE-side tactile input · Joint action–contact prediction**<br>[InternW0: A Foundational Physical World Model for Efficient Real-World Interactions](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.27656v1)<br>Jisong Cai, Yao Mu, Ganlin Yang, Zhe Cao, Zhangzheng Tu, Xing Gao, Kailin Li, Xinyu Zhan, Lixin Yang, Yangkun Zhu, Haoxiang Ma, Ming Zhou, Qiaojun Yu, Yufei Xue, Liqun He, Yifei Yao, Yifan Zhu, Long Ling, Bingqi Jiang, Haoyu Guo, Xueyue Zhu, Bowen Zhou, Bin Zhao, Tianfan Xue, Chunhua Shen, Weinan Zhang<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `parallel-gripper` `wam` `asynchronous-inference` `observation-conditioned-routing` `kv-cache-editing` `action-expert` [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `force-feedback` `tactile-post-training` `joint-action-contact-prediction` `flow-matching` `human-video-pretraining` `cross-embodiment` `laboratory-manipulation` `real-world` `simulation` | InternW0 adds observed force/tactile history to the action expert of a pretrained WAM, jointly denoises future actions and contact signals with flow matching, and decodes the action channels for execution so that subsequent actions incorporate contact feedback.<br>**Evaluation scope:** AE means Action Expert, not autoencoder. Heterogeneous pretraining uses about 7,200 hours of robot and human egocentric data, including about 275 hours of EgoLab: robot trajectories supervise video and action flow matching, while human videos supervise future video only, without requiring tactile labels. Contact-aware post-training extends the action-side inputs with measured force/tactile history and the targets with joint action–contact prediction. Only history observed before generation is supplied; future contact channels are noised and denoised jointly with actions. Action channels execute, so predicted contact must not be assumed to be a directly issued force-control target. The slow video expert exposes layerwise K/V; current DINOv3 image features query and residually edit a chunk-specific context view without cumulatively rewriting the base cache or updating weights online. Asynchronous scheduling and observation-guided routing follow AHA-WAM. Real experiments comprise four tasks with dual parallel-gripper arms and five-stage pipetting with a 20-DoF dexterous hand on a 7-DoF arm; the hand model is unspecified, and paired same-task cross-hand transfer is not established. Each of the five tasks has 15 trials. Pipetting achieves 65.3% ordered-subtask progress, with 46.7% reaching the final stage, rather than 65.3% full-episode success. RTX 5090D latency of 60.73 ms / 16.47 Hz measures only the action critical path, excluding asynchronous video prediction. Official code and Base, RoboTwin-clean and LIBERO weight links are public; the RoboTwin-clean .pt listing was verified. The repository explicitly excludes the paper’s force/tactile, real-robot and laboratory assets; downloadable tactile post-training data, specialized weights and real-robot interfaces have not been verified. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.27656v1) · [Project](https://internrobotics.github.io/internw0/) · [Code](https://github.com/InternRobotics/InternW0) · [Assets](https://huggingface.co/collections/InternRobotics/nternw0) | Initial reading<br>2026-11-04 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.TACTILE.POSTTRAIN.2] <a id="am-man-dex-tactile-posttrain-2"></a> | **VisForce｜VLA architecture · Visual force input to VLM · Current and desired force visualization**<br>[VisForce: Visual Grounding of Current and Desired Forces for Goal-Conditioned Dexterous Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.25785v1)<br>Jung-Woo Lee, Soo-Chul Lim<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` [vla](../../../topics/vla.md) [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `force-feedback` `actuator-force` `force-visualization` `desired-force-conditioning` `fingertip-alignment` `visual-goal-conditioning` `cross-attention` `pi-0-5` `supervised-fine-tuning` `lora` `flow-matching` `real-world` | VisForce renders current actuator forces and desired forces at the corresponding fingertips in the current wrist image and a goal image, conditioning π₀.₅ through vision on both grasp configuration and force magnitude to generate arm–hand actions under the desired-force condition.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Current five-finger actuator forces are rendered as arrows at fingertip locations using a MuJoCo hand model aligned with the real wrist camera and predefined fingertip normals, then overlaid on live images. Arrows encode actuator-force magnitude, not measured 3D contact-force vectors. Goal images are selected from reference demonstrations, foreground-isolated and augmented with predefined desired forces offline, then retrieved for the user-specified current subtask. Shared SigLIP features fuse current wrist queries with foreground goal tokens through cross-attention before entering the VLM and action expert; force enters through vision rather than a separate force encoder. Training fully updates SigLIP and cross-attention, uses LoRA for the VLM and AE, and retains the flow-matching loss. Outputs are 12D joint increments: six UR10 arm joints plus six RH56F1 hand channels, not direct force-control commands. T1 evaluates force-conditioned grasping; T2–T4 evaluate cup insertion/bottle pouring, tong-assisted bread transfer and slip-modulated peg-in-hole. Each policy has 20 trials per task; final cumulative success on T2–T4 is 70%, 55% and 40%. Users specify the current subtask, so autonomous task planning is not established; cross-hand generalization is not evaluated. Code, dataset and checkpoint downloads have not been verified. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.25785v1) | Initial reading<br>2026-11-04 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.TACTILE.POSTTRAIN.3] <a id="am-man-dex-tactile-posttrain-3"></a> | **STAR｜VLA architecture · Pretrained tactile encoder into VLM · Sparse–global tactile representation**<br>[STAR: Sparse Tactile Representation Learning in Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Models for Dexterous Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.12549v1)<br>Xiangcheng Liu, Tianhao Wu, Le Zheng, Yidong Wang, Bowen Jiang, Mingjie Pan, Xinlin Ren, Yi Liu, Jianlan Luo<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` [vla](../../../topics/vla.md) `vtla` [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `pi-0-5` `pretrained-tactile-encoder` `vlm-tactile-input` `visual-tactile-masked-pretraining` `sparse-global-tactile-tokens` `contact-gating` `future-tactile-auxiliary-supervision` `supervised-fine-tuning` `flow-matching` `real-world` | STAR first trains a tactile encoder with joint visual–tactile masked reconstruction, then feeds its activated local and global tactile tokens into the π₀.₅ VLM, using auxiliary future-touch supervision to train an arm–hand policy that exploits sparse contact information.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Tactile-encoder pretraining is a prerequisite for extending an existing VLA; primary placement is Post-training for tactile integration and policy adaptation. MAE-style joint reconstruction uses nonzero tactile frames and paired wrist images from the collected 200-hour dataset, independently masking 75% of patches in each modality. During policy training, each hand produces 196 local patch tokens plus one global token, projected into the VLM prefix alongside visual/language tokens. Contact gating masks inactive local tokens while keeping global tokens attendable. Global tactile tokens cannot attend to visual/language/action tokens, but other modalities can attend to them. The VLM and action expert initialize from π₀.₅ and jointly finetune on 200 hours of multi-task demonstrations, with the tactile encoder also updated, before post-training on 100 demonstrations per task. Auxiliary MLPs predict normal-force patches at future steps 10/20/30/40/50 from local VLM tactile outputs, excluding the global token; actions still use flow matching and predicted touch is not a direct force-control command. The 64D action interface has 34 active dimensions: two 7D end-effector poses and two 10D hand-joint vectors, with zero padding rather than 64 actuated joints. The bimanual wheeled platform has hands with 10 actuated and 16 total DoF each, with 268 piezoresistive taxels covering palms/inner fingers but not finger edges. The dataset has 10,576 trajectories across 65 tasks; 69.5% of trajectories involve dexterous multi-finger manipulation. Supporting data remain in this paper record. Four real-robot tasks cover earbud flipping, stacked-book retrieval, postcard retrieval and multi-object grasping, with 20 trials per policy/task and about 61% mean success. Evaluation objects are absent from the 200-hour dataset but used during task-specific post-training, so this is not zero-shot object generalization. Cross-hand/sensor transfer and uniformly positive tactile gains are not established. Code, dataset and checkpoint downloads have not been verified. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.12549v1) | Initial reading<br>2026-11-04 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.TACTILE.POSTTRAIN.4] <a id="am-man-dex-tactile-posttrain-4"></a> | **DeCAL｜Unified MoT model · VLM-side tactile gating · WM joint future visual–tactile prediction**<br>[DeCAL: Towards Physically-Grounded Dexterous Vision-Language-Action Models via Contact-Aware Latent Co-Imagination](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.09119v1)<br>Yankai Fu, Ning Chen, Junkai Zhao, Heng Zhang, Guocai Yao, Pengwei Wang, Zhongyuan Wang, Shanghang Zhang<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` [vla](../../../topics/vla.md) `vtla` `mixture-of-transformers` [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `tactile-post-training` `vlm-tactile-input` `contact-aware-gating` `visuo-tactile-world-model` `future-tactile-prediction` `latent-co-imagination` `factorized-flow-matching` `flow-matching` `imitation-learning` `supervised-fine-tuning` `action-chunking` `real-world` | DeCAL extends a pretrained VLA with contact-aware gating that injects fingertip touch into the VLM and joint prediction of future visual and tactile latents; conditioned on these predictions, its action expert generates manipulation actions through factorized arm–hand flow matching with joint coordination.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Initialized from InternVLA-A1-3B, DeCAL jointly trains visual foresight, tactile reconstruction and flow-matching actions on robot demonstrations, supporting placement under tactile post-training. The MoT contains understanding, generation and action Transformer experts with directional information flow, rather than three independent agents. At deployment, shared ResNet and cross-finger Transformer layers encode fingertip deformation maps into local/global tactile tokens: local tokens enter the VLM through cross-attention, while the global token controls the gate. Encoded current per-finger 6D force/torque also conditions the generation expert's future visual–tactile latents. Training uses future visual latents, raw tactile images, deformation maps and 6D force targets; reconstruction decoders are omitted at inference, and predicted touch is not a direct force-control command. The action expert conditions on understanding features, predicted latents and proprioception. Arm/hand actions start from separate noise distributions and token projections, then are jointly processed into 50-step chunks, without RL or online weight updates. Observation history includes 15 preceding frames and the current frame. The real platform uses dual UR5 arms and two 22-DoF SharpaWave hands with vision-based fingertip tactile sensors; 6D force/torque is regressed from tactile images. Six tasks cover vase wiping, whiteboard erasing, part assembly, cap unscrewing, pipetting and bulb screwing, with 100 demonstrations per task and 20 evaluation trials per method/task by default. Cross-hand transfer is not established. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.09119v1) · [Project](https://aureleopku.github.io/DeCAL/) | Initial reading<br>2026-11-04 |
